newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil c/acct gap widens to 4.2 pct/GDP in June.
newsitem.headline: Brazil c/acct gap widens to 4.2 pct/GDP in June.

text.p: The deficit in Brazil's balance of payments current account in the 12 months to June was $32.289 billion, or 4.19 percent of gross domestic product, the Central Bank said.
The bank said in a statement that the 12-month current account gap had widened slightly from 4.07 percent of GDP in the 12-month period ending in May.
The bank said that in the first half of the year, the current account deficit amounted to $15.621 billion against $7.679 billion in the same year-ago period.

The bank also said foreign direct investment in the first half of 1997 was $7.382 billion compared with $4.857 billion in the first half of 1996. It added that foreign direct investment covered 47.3 percent of the year-to-date current account gap.

It also said net foreign reserves edged down to $56.795 billion in June from $58.459 billion in May. According to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable, the reserves were $57.615 billion in June against $59.279 billion the previous month.
Altamir Lopes, the head of the bank's economics department was due to brief journalists shortly.
